operations_plan.summary: Make the main U-shaped open-jaw cutout 10 mm shallower by adding material at its closed throat. Translate the effective throat profile 10 mm toward the jaw mouth in the global -Z direction while preserving the two parallel gripping faces at x=-10 mm and x=10 mm, their exact 20 mm separation, the existing 5 mm throat blends, the jaw tips, the external head profile, and the 15 mm part thickness. This resolves the depth-direction ambiguity using the interpretation specified in aim.json: move the deepest throat boundary toward the open mouth rather than changing the mouth or wrench size.

steps.description: Identify the open-ended wrench head and recover the existing internal cutout profile in the X-Z planform. Use the left and right parallel jaw faces, face 20 at x=-10 mm and face 22 at x=10 mm, as the functional size references. Confirm that their perpendicular separation is 20 mm. Identify the current closed throat as transverse root face 18 at approximately z=-110 mm, joined to the parallel faces by the 5 mm-radius cylindrical blends 19 and 17. Record the current blend tangency locations at approximately z=-115 mm and the mouth/jaw-tip end at approximately z=-150 mm. The requested 10 mm shallowing direction is global -Z, toward the open mouth.

Create a sketch on the global X-Z plane, or on a planar face parallel to it, using the existing open-jaw edges as projected references. Construct a closed reinforcement profile representing the portion of the existing void that must become solid. Use the original throat boundary formed by faces 19, 18, and 17 as one boundary. Construct the desired new throat boundary 10 mm toward the mouth in global -Z: place the new transverse root at z=-120 mm and reproduce the two existing 5 mm-radius tangent blends so that they meet the left and right jaw lines at approximately z=-125 mm. Constrain the left and right jaw lines to x=-10 mm and x=10 mm, respectively, so their separation remains exactly 20 mm. Close the reinforcement profile with line segments along those jaw lines between the old tangency positions near z=-115 mm and the new tangency positions near z=-125 mm. This profile must lie entirely inside the original cutout and must not intersect or alter the external open-head perimeter.

Extrude the closed reinforcement profile through the complete body thickness and join it to solid 0. The extrusion must span exactly from the bottom body plane at y=0, face 25, to the top body plane at y=15, face 24, using a 15 mm through-thickness additive extrusion or an equivalent up-to-face extent. Boolean-union the extrusion with the existing monolithic body. The added material fills the rear 10 mm of the original jaw cutout while leaving the mouth open. Do not extend the extrusion beyond either broad body face and do not modify the shallow handle recess.

Regenerate and heal the joined solid so coincident coplanar faces are merged. The portions of jaw faces 20 and 22 between approximately z=-115 mm and z=-125 mm are consumed by the added material, leaving parallel gripping flats from the mouth to the new blend tangencies. The resulting internal cutout must terminate at the reconstructed throat near z=-120 mm with two tangent 5 mm-radius root blends. Preserve the original through-thickness condition of all remaining cutout walls. No chamfers, fillets, or offsets are to be applied to the jaw flats or outer head.

Validate the regenerated model. Measure the perpendicular distance between the surviving parallel internal jaw surfaces and confirm it is exactly 20 mm. Measure cutout depth from the unchanged jaw-tip/mouth datum near z=-150 mm to the deepest throat point and confirm that it is 10 mm less than the original depth, with the deepest throat location shifted from approximately z=-110 mm to z=-120 mm. Confirm the external open-head faces 9, 15, 16, and 23, the jaw-tip positions, the handle and recessed panel, the ring end and bore, and the y=0 to y=15 overall thickness remain unchanged. Confirm that the result is one valid watertight solid with no unintended internal slivers or disconnected bodies.
